record_notes.DCP-LETT-1820A: January 14, supplied 1856. Proposal for an accompanied library consultation is not an event already completed. Source has doubled punctuation specified.. held for supported final cleanup. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1822A: January 19, supplied 1856. Two blocks and single footnote read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1915: July 1, supplied 1856. Three blocks, two notes and bibliography read. Requests disjunct north/south distributions of echinoderm species or representative genera lacking tropical counterparts, explicitly ignorant of actual ranges. Prior offer to help does not identify a written prompt. Absence of Gray name from later manuscript bibliography is not proof no reply occurred; no source-complete incoming answer in current pool.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1877: May 27, supplied 1856. Four full blocks, five footnotes and bibliography read. Supports Huxley for London University examinership after an unlocated request, supplies contemporary qualifications, and asks the elder John William Lubbock to consult his son John. Explicitly says no answer required. July 9 appointment is later editorial outcome, not current knowledge. After-closing regret records missed dinner yesterday, distinct from projected influence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1880: Dated only day 28, with 104 discrete month/year alternatives from June 1856 through January 1865. Two blocks and full explanatory footnote read. File position and recipient death constrain conjecture, not actual month/year; 1865 illness report does not prove present date. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1990: November 18, supplied 1856. Three blocks and three notes read. Missing elder Lubbock note acknowledged; forwarding to Wedgwood and discussion of admission cards are intended next acts. A. Woods furniture misunderstanding corrected in body; Sarah Wedgwood December 9 auction linkage probable editorial identification, not body naming or current auction completion. November 20 payment does not date prior letter delivery.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1930: July 18, 1856. Two blocks, footnote and bibliography read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1013: October 27, supplied 1856, despite older catalogue-number position and earlier publication under conjectured 1846/1848. Two blocks, three footnotes and bibliography read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1829A: February 6, supplied 1856. Two blocks and three notes read. Missing Birch note offers assistance; London call in a fortnight is planned and does not prove execution. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1841A: Supplied March 12,1856, body dateline Wednesday; two blocks, two notes and bibliography read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-13867A: December 7 in1855/1856/1857 alternatives with questioned date range in title. Two blocks, three notes and bibliography read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1972: October 9, supplied1856. Three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1196: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. August 26, 1848 autograph draft. Gray answers recent misunderstanding communicated by Darwin, recalls earlier synonym help request, explains catalogue papers intended to facilitate Darwin work and says he will withdraw unpublished papers. Postscript excepts two March papers already in type. His claims of oral credit and specimen illustrations conflict with or exceed later printed-text evidence in editorial note; preserve the historical self-report without silently correcting it. P4 recalls 1155 request, but immediate occasion is recent interview and cannot be reduced to a February-to-August reply pair. 1197 explicitly answers this reconciliation letter, though draft wording is not automatically the exact delivered text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1197: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Distinctive anticipation dispute, assurances and synonym acknowledgment identify 1196, not general barnacle topic. Oral discussion and unidentified critics are additional inputs. Future publication of acknowledgment and informing critics are intentions, not completed acts. Draft-versus-sent-text difference remains an export hold.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1536: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 11, supplied 1853 ALS. Five blocks and five full footnotes. Missing Lubbock note received this morning; Darwin infers agreement from oral remarks but sees risk project fails if deed altered. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1563: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 28, supplied 1854 ALS. Five blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Innes nomination not school trusteeship; Darwin own declined candidacy separate. Vestry attendance tomorrow prospective, no election outcome. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1628: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January 10, supplied 1855 ALS. Three blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. January 9 long oral interview with Baugh reported; Darwin fears little success. Workmen stopped by Lubbock report; conversion to cottages and reinvestment conditional future, not actual conversion. Baugh complaint of prior ignorance until September is his claim. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1631: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Monday 15, supplied January 1855 ALS. Four blocks and two footnotes. Further Court of Equity and local law-cost subscription conditional; lawyer opinion reported through Baugh, not court judgment. Archbishop not discussed explicitly. London house taken, Thursday move and scientific meetings future, later itinerary not proof current attendance.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1812: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Unaddressed draft memorandum, assigned December 1855; seven extracted blocks, twenty footnotes, bibliography and complete raw broken-list markup read. reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
